newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Alusaf trying to make Mozal project viable.
newsitem.headline: Alusaf trying to make Mozal project viable.

text.p: Aluminium producer Alusaf Ltd has signed a "housekeeping" agreement with Mozambique on the proposed $1.2 billion Mozal aluminium smelter but is still trying to cut costs to make the project commercially viable, Alusaf managing director Rob Barbour said on Monday.
Barbour signed a heads of agreement with the Mozambican government last Thursday.

"It's simply a matter of housekeeping, in that it acknowledges that during the (feasibility) study...we had agreed between the parties that the Mozambique government would do certain things to enable the project to happen.
"This agreement simply documents those things. It in no way commits the project, it is all subject to the project going ahead," Barbour told Reuters.

Brian Gilbertson, chairman of Gencor Ltd, which owns Alusaf, said last month that a study into the project had been completed and proved the smelter to be feasible, but returns were not attractive enough yet.
Barbour said the Alusaf team studying the Mozal smelter had been sent back to the drawing board.
"The study group has been sent back to the drawing board to go and try and do better. So we'll be talking to all aspects of the project, trying to get the financial numbers looking better".
